critical_code_review_comments: translateUserInput is called from ShopSignoffCard line 69 + PartsCatalog lines 138 & 442 — wire-up matches iter15-16 pattern across the original 5 forms. The walker in /app/frontend/src/lib/translateOnSubmit.js correctly skips numeric/yes-no/photo/signature/date/_count fields via SKIP_KEY_RE so identifiers, photos, and timestamps stay untranslated.

GET /api/equipment-inspections aggregation (server.py:2083-2123) computes cleared as `fail_count>0 AND signoff_count>=fail_count` — correct semantics. Note: cleared is FALSE when fail_count==0 (no fails to clear), which means inspections that PASSED outright also show no green badge. Frontend should treat 'no FAIL' rows as already-OK rather than 'not cleared' — confirmed EquipmentDashboard.jsx + ShopHub.jsx only render the badge when fail_count>0 AND signoff_count>=fail_count, so this is handled correctly client-side.

_create_safety_indexes() (server.py:4286) creates indexes on every backend startup via Mongo's create_index (idempotent). All 12 indexes target the right query patterns (created_at sort, equipment_unit lookup, severity filter, unit_number unique). Good defensive design — log line '[safety-indexes] ensured' confirmed in supervisor backend.err.log on every restart since 2026-04-28 15:45.

i18n.js _syncHtmlLang() runs on init AND on every setLang() call — verified in playwright test: html.lang='en' on /, click ES button -> 'es', reload -> still 'es' (persisted via localStorage 'masci.lang'), click EN -> 'en'. Zero inputs override the html-level lang attribute, so browser-native spellcheck dictionary will swap correctly.

TranslateRequest payload shape is {strings: {...}, from_lang, to_lang} — NOT {text, source, target} as the review_request example implied. Both the frontend translateUserInput and the iter24 pytest correctly use the strings-dict shape. Documented in this report so future testing agents do not waste cycles on wrong shape.
